# Performance PASS: #228 / F186

Exact head **`b0259b1987d3f829e5494cefa9e366d07404544b`**. Detached review tree clean; GitHub CLEAN and checks green. Jordan's 2026-11-11 ruling is verified at governance `f078301c`, `.harness/government/handover/prime-preferences.md:9`: nice-19-only replaces background taskpolicy and the automatic F63 compile/run split.

**The changed launchers implement that policy, without a daemon/runtime-loop change.** No local build, test, install or live probe was run; CI is the execution proof. No machine-build baton was requested or consumed.

| Invocation | New behavior and cost delta |
|---|---|
| Build/check/other supplied cargo command | One supplied cargo invocation under nice 19. Where the old taskpolicy wrapper existed, that wrapper image is removed; this is not a measured reduction in unique PIDs or whole-machine launch rate. |
| Ordinary `cargo test` | Two cargo invocations (compile-only, then run) become one nice-only invocation as supplied. The generated `--no-run` argument preparation, extra cargo/nice invocation and between-phase disk check disappear. Tests previously executed once, **not twice**; the removed phase was compilation-only. |
| `cargo test --doc` | Remains one nice-only invocation, with no incompatible generated `--no-run`. Explicit caller arguments are passed through, including an explicit compile-only request. |
| `route-inventory-check` | The separate compile wrapper is gone; one `/usr/bin/nice -n 19 cargo test ... route_inventory_tests` remains. It still executes the inventory test once. |

`shared-build` keeps its physical-target mkdir lock for the whole `--then` batch, the 25-GiB default floor and per-command checks, source freshness handling, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, stale-owner reporting without auto-clearing, cargo status propagation and process-group draining before unlock. The default cargo and libtest caps remain four via the script/config; existing explicit environment/test-thread/cargo overrides remain, so four is not a newly enforced universal hard ceiling.

The existing waiting loop is unchanged: default 20-second polls per waiting caller, with df/mkdir/sleep work; no work when the wrapper is not invoked. No new timer, sweep or per-seat launch. All eight changed files are build wrappers, fixtures, documentation/ledger material, or Rust documentation comments (`testkit::time`); there is no daemon logic or production timing-constant change. `scaled()` and `PIJ_TEST_TIME_SCALE` remain.

**Scheduling scope:** removing background QoS makes performance-core execution available and removes that explicit I/O throttle. `nice` sets priority; it does not pin a core, guarantee a wall-clock speedup, or cap all descendant threads/processes at four. The existing absent-nice fallback is unchanged; the real fleet/CI normal path uses `/usr/bin/nice`, and CI checks the resulting priority.

**The newer machine-wide rule also applies:** per otter's 2026-11-11 10:25 ruling packet, any future heavy local build/test needs the `machine-build` baton granted by its keeper first, and returned immediately afterward with its observed lease id. The per-target artifact lock is not that cross-project authorization. This read-only CI-backed review starts no such run.

**CI proof:** [run 42929038558](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42929038558), successful at the requested head. [Node 22 job 130222812819](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42929038558/job/130222812819) explicitly tests merge `fe1705af35b856a0927849b85a81b16eb913cfcd`, this head into `5f9727e984c2cb86cb09c34a5ecd758f479f01d0`. Existing lock, floor, jobs, signal-drain and batch cases execute in that file. Vitest total: **2,289 passed, six skips separately**. Node 24 and Rust checks are also green.
